---
title: LruCache
description: The small, dependency-free least-recently-used map that backs the memory tier.
---

## Purpose

`LruCache<K, V>` in `packages/i18n/src/cache/lru.ts` is a bounded `Map` that evicts the least
recently used entry when it grows past its capacity. It is the only cache primitive in the package;
`MemoryStore` composes it.

## When to Use It

Use it directly when you need a bounded, in-memory cache with the same semantics. Applications rarely
touch it; every namespace load path in the runtime goes through `MemoryStore`, which is an
`LruCache` keyed by `"<lng>:<ns>"`.

## Usage

```ts
import { LruCache } from '@faang/i18n'

const cache = new LruCache<string, number>(2)
cache.set('a', 1)
cache.set('b', 2)
cache.get('a') // 1 — 'a' is now the most recently used
cache.set('c', 3) // evicts 'b'
cache.has('b') // false
```

## API

| Member | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `new LruCache` | `(capacity: number)` | throws `RangeError` if not an integer `>= 1` |
| `get` | `(key: K) => V \| undefined` | marks the key most-recently-used |
| `set` | `(key: K, value: V) => void` | inserts and evicts from the front until under capacity |
| `has` | `(key: K) => boolean` | does not change recency |
| `delete` | `(key: K) => boolean` | returns whether the key existed |
| `size` | `() => number` | current entry count |
| `keys` | `() => K[]` | keys from least to most recently used |

## Parameters and Returns

`capacity` must be an integer greater than or equal to 1. `get` returns `undefined` for a miss and
otherwise the stored reference (values are not cloned). `keys` returns a snapshot array; mutating it
does not affect the cache.

## Behavior and Edge Cases

- Recency is defined by `get` and `set`: a `get` hit deletes and re-inserts the entry, moving it to
  the back of the underlying `Map`'s insertion order.
- `has` performs a plain membership check and does **not** refresh recency.
- `set` on an existing key updates the value and refreshes recency rather than duplicating.
- Eviction is a `while` loop, so a `set` after shrinking the capacity conceptually still trims to the
  configured capacity (capacity is immutable after construction).
- The store holds references, not deep copies. Mutating a cached value mutates what callers receive.

## Failure Modes

The constructor is the only thrower: a non-integer, `0`, or negative capacity raises `RangeError`.
All other operations are total.
